item.title: Phantom Billstickers founder and Christchurch music scene heavyweight dies
item.description: The company said Jim Wilson passed away peacefully in his sleep, of natural causes.

item.title: Luxury electric vehicle brand ArcFox set for NZ
item.description: Auto Distributors NZ set to add another Chinese carmaker to its roster following BAIC launch.

item.title: School warns students of strangers after attempted kidnapping
item.description: A student at St Joseph’s Catholic School was biking to school when they were approached by a man.

item.title: Van Gisbergen’s shot at NASCAR history denied as Michael Jordan’s team claims three-peat
item.description: Tyler Reddick makes NASCAR history with third straight win to start the season.

item.title: Charges laid over the sinking of Navy ship off Samoa’s coast
item.description: Three officers are facing charges in the Court Martial in connection to the ship’s sinking in 2024.

item.title: More than 19 line and tube failures raise alarm in medical child abuse trial
item.description: A child at the centre of a medical abuse trial experienced at least 19 failures of feeding tubes and central lines, a High Court has heard.

item.title: Luxon: NZ ‘not best placed’ to pass judgement on US and Israel
item.description: The PM said New Zealand was “not party or proxy” to intelligence held by the Americans and Israelis that might have influenced their decision to launch strikes.

item.title: Man in custody after ‘large number’ of armed police descend on rural community
item.description: A local resident said she saw around 10 police cars and 15 armed police on Mellsop Rd around 1.30pm.

item.title: Kiwi injured during Middle East strikes waits in Dubai for way home
item.description: A New Zealander caught up in the escalating tensions in the Middle East says he is now waiting in Dubai after being injured when explosions began while he was riding a scooter.

item.title: Would NZ join ‘an illegal invasion’ of Iran? That question needs to be asked, Helen Clark says
item.description: Speaking to Stuff’s Samantha Hayes, Clark said she would “very much hope” that New Zealand does not militarily supporting what she called an “illegal invasion”.
